title: Why is every rainbow the same size? 10,000 rays into one drop pile up at 42.4 degrees, none past it.
description:
Why is every rainbow the same size? 10,000 parallel rays of red light enter one round water drop at evenly spaced heights from the centre to the top edge. Each ray bends going in (Snell's law), bounces once off the back of the drop, and bends again coming out. The exit direction is measured from the antisolar direction, the line straight back toward the sun. Exact geometry: vector refraction and reflection, no time step, no seed. Then the same 10,000 rays as violet light.

Measured:
- red (n = 1.331): the exit angles pile up at 42.37 degrees (closed form 4 asin(sin i0 / n) - 2 i0 with cos^2 i0 = (n^2 - 1) / 3 gives 42.370); ray 8,619 of 10,000, at 0.862 of the radius, reaches it; 1,196 of the 10,000 rays leave within one degree of the pile and 375 within a tenth of a degree; 0 rays leave past 42.37 degrees; the centre ray leaves at 0.00 degrees, the edge ray at 15.95
- violet (n = 1.343): the pile is at 40.65 degrees (closed form 40.646); 1,237 rays within one degree; 0 past it; the two piles are 1.72 degrees apart, and the band between them is the bow, red outside, violet inside
- two bounces (the secondary bow, not drawn): red piles at 50.37 degrees and violet at 53.48; no ray of either kind leaves between the first pile and the second, the dark band outside the main bow

Why: the exit angle grows with the height of the ray, stops growing at 42.37 degrees, and turns back toward the edge. Near the turning point many rays leave at almost the same angle, so a distant eye sees a bright ring 42 degrees from the antisolar point, no matter how far away the drops are. The histogram on screen counts rays in half-degree bins of exit direction. Counts are of rays, not brightness: the run ignores the light that reflects off the surface or leaks out at the back.

Rerun sims/rainbow/rainbow.py with projects/rainbow/manifest.json and you get these numbers exactly.

Made end to end by an AI agent: simulation, footage, voice, music, and edit.
